## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`status()` shortens the revision to 7 characters while `history()` and `completed()` use 12, even though its docstring says it uses the same identifier as history. This should be fixed so the running status matches the other deployment output.

## Changes
The pull request adds `status(revision, attempt)` and `attempt_label(attempt)` to `app/display.py`, which build a "Running: <revision> (attempt N)" line. It also adds tests for both functions in `tests/test_display.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — Use `revision[:12]` in `status()` to match history — For `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef..."`, `status(REVISION, 2)` returns `Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)` while `history(REVISION)` returns `History: 0123456789ab`. Your docstring at line 13 says "using the same identifier as history", but `history()` and `completed()` both slice `[:12]` (lines 5 and 9). — Operators matching a running deployment to its history or completion line get a different, shorter revision ID in the status line. — Fix: Change to `revision[:12]` and extend `test_running_status_contains_attempt` to assert the full expected string, because its `startswith`/`endswith` checks never look at the revision.
